newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real slips 0.01 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real slips 0.01 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.01 percent to end at 1.0276 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank set a weaker mini-band for the currency of 1.0275 to 1.0325 per dollar, dealers said.
The Central Bank set the new trading level for the fluctuation of the real by buying dollars at 1.0275 reais and selling at 1.0325 reais in a morning auction.
The Central Bank bought dollars at 1.0275 reais per U.S. unit to drain excess dollars from the market in the late afternoon.
The previous mini-band, set Thursday, was between 1.0265 and 1.0315 reais to the dollar.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real dropped 0.12 percent to end at 1.0331 to the dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed steady at 1.095 to the dollar, traders said.
